_use: A-story module for investigation/conspiracy thrillers. A plot-mode layer, not a spine. Works with any archetype. Climb one rung per tier in order; roll scheme, clock, and red herring once per episode. Shared by two consumers: episode-scale into the plot generator's Investigation toggle, season-scale into the C-Story Engine as a conspiracy spine type whose five rungs become the C-clicks the Season Shaper distributes.
scheme: The visible crime is cover for a theft no one has noticed yet.
The target is being framed so the real culprit can act unwatched.
An inside faction is selling out the institution from within.
A loss is being manufactured to justify a seizure of power.
A far larger crime is being laundered through this small one.
The threat is real but aimed at a different victim than everyone assumes.

tier_1_surface: The presented threat does not add up; the timeline is wrong.
A detail at the scene was planted, not left behind.
The first victim was a message, not the point.
tier_2_scope: This is one of several identical cases no one had connected.
The operation reaches into an institution the hero trusted.
The money or cargo trail runs far past the local players.
tier_3_betrayal: Someone feeding the hero information is feeding the other side too.
An ally's alibi is the one piece of the story that was fabricated.
The hero's own side authorized the thing the hero is trying to stop.
tier_4_personal: The hero was handed this case because they were expected to fail.
The scheme needs the hero's own action to complete; they are the tool.
The wound in the hero's past was the opening move of this same plan.
tier_5_true_stakes: When the clock runs out, the real target, not the decoy, is taken.
The deadline is the moment the cover becomes permanent, not a moment to act.
Stopping it now exposes the hero as the one who let it get this far.

clock: A handoff at a fixed hour that cannot be moved.
A vote, ruling, or signature that locks the scheme in once it passes.
A witness who will be gone, bought, or silenced by a set time.
A shipment in transit that becomes untouchable on arrival.
A cover story that becomes unbreakable once it is filed.
red_herring: The obvious suspect is guilty of something, just not this.
A planted document points the hero confidently the wrong way.
A second, louder crime pulls attention while the real one proceeds.
A defector offers help that burns the hero's most expensive hours.
step_behind: The antagonist acts on the exact lead the hero just uncovered.
Every door the hero opens was left open on purpose.
The hero's progress is the antagonist's timeline; catching up is the plan.
